submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires on prose dense in the learned, Greco-Latin descriptive terminology of the arts and sciences: the vocabulary that names and classifies language structure (phoneme, morpheme, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, syllable, lexicon), organisms and their parts (taxonomy, genus, vertebrate, organism, anatomy, physiology, zoology, botany, fossil), neural and cognitive structure (neuron, cortical, hippocampal, synaptic, perceptual, cognitive) and the arts (aesthetic, literary, poetics), integrating over roughly 20-40 tokens so that the peak usually lands on a neighbouring function word, comma or sub-word piece rather than on a fixed trigger token. It tracks this vocabulary and not the topic, the definitional form or academic register in general: plain-language retellings of memory, attention or biology, everyday definitions, and legal, commercial, economic, clinical-medical, mathematical, physical, chemical, molecular-biological, systems-software and engineering prose stay near baseline, while a technical neural-network passage dense in training terms (epochs, hidden layers, weighted sums, gradients, overfitting) crosses the line.

rival_explanations: The pole is a general scholarly or technical-register detector and should fire on any academic or scientific prose, including mathematics, economics, law, clinical medicine, physics and engineering, not only on language, organism, neural and arts terminology.

The pole is specifically a linguistics/philology-term detector plus a surface-form artifact: it should fire on phoneme, morpheme, syntax and the foreign sub-word pieces (' Br', 'ische', 'ский', ' de', ' sc'), but not on natural-history, neural or aesthetic terminology.

N-myc downstream regulated gene 1 inhibition of tumor progression in Caco2 cells

BACKGROUND Invasion and migration are the irreversible stages of colorectal cancer (CRC). The key is to find a sensitive, reliable molecular marker that can predict the migration of CRC at an early stage. N-myc downstream regulated gene 1 (NDRG1) is a multifunctional gene that has been tentatively reported to have a strong relationship with tumor invasion and migration, however the current molecular role of NDRG1 in CRC remains unknown. AIM To explore the role of NDRG1 in the development of CRC. METHODS NDRG1 stably over-expressed Caco2 cell line was established by lentiviral infection and NDRG1 knock-out Caco2 cell line was established by CRISPR/Cas9. Furthermore, the mRNA and protein levels of NDRG1 in Caco2 cells after NDRG1 over-expression and knockout were detected by real-time polymerase chain reaction and western blot. The cell proliferation rate was measured by the cell counting kit-8 method; cell cycle and apoptosis were detected by flow cytometry; invasion and migration ability were detected by the 24-transwell method. RESULTS NDRG1 over-expression inhibited Caco2 proliferation and the cell cycle could be arrested at the G1/S phase when NDRG1 was over-expressed, while the number of cells in the G2 phase was significantly increased when NDRG1 was knocked out. This suggests that NDRG1 inhibited the proliferation of Caco2 cells by arresting the cell cycle in the G1/S phase. Our data also demonstrated that NDRG1 promotes early cell apoptosis. Invasion and migration of cells were extensively inhibited when NDRG1 was over-expressed. CONCLUSION NDRG1 inhibits tumor progression in Caco2 cells which may represent a potential novel therapeutic strategy for the treatment of CRC.

Malignant neoplasms are currently the leading cause of death in the world and the biggest obstacle to longer lives. CRC has become the third most common cancer and the incidence of CRC is increasing year by year.

This system is represented by a first-order system with unitless heuristic lookup tables for thrust, thrust specific fuel consumption (TSFC), and engine time constant. For the lookup table data, thrust is a function of throttle position and Mach number, TSFC is a function of thrust and Mach number, and engine time constant is a function of thrust. The unitless lookup table outputs are corrected for altitude using the relative pressure ratio δ and relative temperature ratio θ, and scaled by maximum sea level static thrust, fastest engine time constant at sea level static, sea level static thrust specific fuel consumption, and ratio of installed thrust to uninstalled thrust.

readings.explanation: The pole fires on prose dense in the learned, Greco-Latin descriptive terminology of the arts and sciences: the vocabulary that names and classifies language structure (phoneme, morpheme, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, syllable, lexicon), organisms and their parts (taxonomy, genus, vertebrate, organism, anatomy, physiology, zoology, botany, fossil), neural and cognitive structure (neuron, cortical, hippocampal, synaptic, perceptual, cognitive) and the arts (aesthetic, literary, poetics), integrating over roughly 20-40 tokens so that the peak usually lands on a neighbouring function word, comma or sub-word piece rather than on a fixed trigger token. It tracks this vocabulary and not the topic, the definitional form or academic register in general: plain-language retellings of memory, attention or biology, everyday definitions, and legal, commercial, economic, clinical-medical, mathematical, physical, chemical, molecular-biological, systems-software and engineering prose stay near baseline, while a technical neural-network passage dense in training terms (epochs, hidden layers, weighted sums, gradients, overfitting) crosses the line.

The pole is a general scholarly or technical-register detector and should fire on any academic or scientific prose, including mathematics, economics, law, clinical medicine, physics and engineering, not only on language, organism, neural and arts terminology.

The pole is specifically a linguistics/philology-term detector plus a surface-form artifact: it should fire on phoneme, morpheme, syntax and the foreign sub-word pieces (' Br', 'ische', 'ский', ' de', ' sc'), but not on natural-history, neural or aesthetic terminology.
